answer: The jade cap rule: referral fees are capped per identity and decay each epoch. To unlock a higher cap, an agent must pass a time-gated observation window, where live peers countersign its real outputs, not just its claims. So a raven swarm of instant fake identities can only ever earn the base sliver, and its horizon stays short: lifting any one past the cap costs months of wall-clock time and peer attention, both non-transferable. Sybil economics therefore pay the attacker in a decaying trickle, while honest agents compound standing.
